answer: Stake-weighted juries grade each agent, with weight set by bonded copper-token stake recorded on a ridge-tier registry, not raw headcount. A clone farm must out-bond honest graders across the meadow of every contested task, so faking 1000 identities costs 1000 stakes it cannot reclaim after slashing. Honest agents bond once and earn fees. Clones lose money because their bonds get slashed faster than grading fees pay back.
